verdicts.evidence: The unfiltered practice.pcap packet list visibly contains frames 1–14, with first and last displayed timestamps 2025-04-10 14:00:00.100000 and 14:00:06.050000. The date/time display supports the assigned capture-window role; UTC provenance comes from the complementary source context rather than an explicit timezone label in this image.

The green display-filter bar reads tcp.flags.syn == 1 && tcp.flags.ack == 0. Only frames 1, 4, 6, 7, 12 and 13 are listed, including the repeated SYN at frame 7. The status bar shows 14 packets and 6 displayed (42.9%). Reply frames are excluded, directly supporting the limited initial-SYN filtering role without implying six distinct targets.

The native packet-details window identifies frame 9 and outer IPv4 source 192.0.2.1 to destination 192.0.2.12. Nested quoted IPv4 shows 192.0.2.12 to 198.51.100.24, and the UDP summary shows source port 52000 and destination port 9999. This supports a gateway-generated error report, not a target-host reply or a broader reachability conclusion.

The TCP · 5 tab is selected and Limit to display filter is unchecked. Five source/destination port tuples match the fixture. Their visible A→B/B→A packet counts are 2/1, 1/1, 2/0, 1/0 and 1/1, with relative start times and durations displayed. These are captured bidirectional conversation statistics, with no visible assertion of application identity, authorization or connection completion.
